empty.title: No scheduled payments
empty.description: Debts to suppliers for received orders with a payment date will appear here.

help.title: How the payment schedule is calculated

items: The supplier debt is their settlements balance (all movements: payments, returns, adjustments), not the sum of orders.

blocks.title: Spreading by dates
items: The debt is spread over unpaid received orders from the oldest payment date; orders the debt does not reach count as paid.

items.text: the payment date has passed or is not set; debt above the orders total goes here too
orders with a payment date in the period

items: The credit limit of purchase agreements is taken off the latest orders.
Click a cell to see the orders that make up the amount.

list.title: Supplier payments
list.emptyDrafts: No drafts — all payments are posted or cancelled

reversal.title: Reverse supplier payment

consequence.common: The {{amount}} payment stays in the list marked “Reversed” and no longer counts: the debt to the supplier grows by this amount, the order’s paid amount decreases, and the exchange difference of its full payment is rolled back.
consequence.bankLine: A payment matched from a bank statement line can only be reversed by unmatching that line — the reversal will not go through here.
consequence.money: No money moves on the account: if the supplier has to return the funds, record that separately.

reversal.reasonPlaceholder: For example: paid to the wrong supplier

confirmDialog.title: Post payment {{number}}?
confirmDialog.message: {{amount}} to supplier "{{supplier}}" will be paid from "{{source}}". A posted payment is not cancelled but reversed: a cash payment in the cash desk, a bank payment with “Reverse” here.

cancelDialog.title: Cancel draft {{number}}?
cancelDialog.message: The draft becomes Cancelled; no money moved, no postings.

list.help: Old drafts (before 2026-10-30 a payment was created and posted in two steps) live here. Post checks the order status, the shift and the cash balance just like a new payment.
